claims.text: Consider the wrapper approach where the budget lifetime is explicitly scoped to the wrapper or ParamsStream rather than using mutable state on streams.
claims.quote: the lifetime of the budget there is just the wrapper, which seems fairly explicit to me?
claims.status_note: author adopted wrapper approach with non-overridable parameter feature
claims.status_by_quote: I've switched to your approach, but added a feature for parameters to declare they cannot be overridden

claims.text: Explain whether the complexity and minimal CPU cost of the last few commits is worth it given other memory-eating places in Bitcoin Core.
claims.quote: Are they really worth the complexity (and minimal cpu cost) when there are other places in Bitcoin Core that can eat memory (including in p2p). Are we going to address all of them?
claims.status_note: author agreed the performance gains did not justify the complexity and dropped all but the first two commits
claims.status_by_quote: I have dropped all but the first two commits; I think it's fair that the performance gains don't justify the complexity

claims.text: Oversized blocks failing deserialization are not disconnected, so the block request stays in mapBlocksInFlight until the 10-minute download timeout expires, potentially stalling block download.
claims.quote: Since the peer isn't disconnected, the hash stays in mapBlocksInFlight until the 10-minute download timeout expires.
claims.status_note: accepted leaving peer disconnect handling to a follow-up
claims.status_by_quote: Makes sense to keep just these two commits and leave peer disconnect handling for undeserializable messages to a follow-

claims.text: Keep block validation reasons covered through submitblock in feature_block.py now that P2P deserialization rejects them earlier
claims.quote: These blocks used to exercise `bad-txns-vin-empty` and `bad-txns-vout-empty`. Now that P2P deserialization stops earlier, sending the same blocks through `submitblock` would keep both checks covered.

claims.text: Add a test checking that outputs survive a TX_NO_WITNESS round trip for zero-input funding templates
claims.quote: A funding template can have outputs before the wallet picks any inputs. I’d check that those outputs survive a `TX_NO_WITNESS` round trip here.

claims.text: Add a release note documenting the new input and output count limits for RPC and kernel callers
claims.quote: This also changes what RPC and kernel callers can inspect. A short release note with the two counts would help explain why a transaction that used to decode now fails.

claims.text: Check flags when reading zero-input transactions so incomplete output data produces an end-of-data error rather than superfluous witness record
claims.quote: Getting `Superfluous witness record` when the output data is incomplete could be confusing for the user, we could also check `flags` here...

claims.text: Share the upper bounds on block input and output counts between UnserializeTransaction and AccessByTxid
claims.quote: `AccessByTxid` already calculates the same output limit. If we move the bounds here, it can reuse `MAX_OUTPUTS_PER_BLOCK`.

claims.text: Leave room above consensus limits so transactions slightly above the limit receive validation errors rather than decode failures
claims.quote: I’d leave some room above the consensus limits - given this is meant to avoid extremes. For the one extra input in this test I’d still expect `bad-txns-oversize` from validation.

claims.text: Whether it makes sense to extract common transaction parsing logic between UnserializeTransaction and PR 36548
claims.quote: Would it make sense to extract the common part here so we only have one place to update these rules?

claims.text: Use expressions naming the serialized field widths rather than magic numbers for the minimum input and output weights
claims.quote: I’d find these minimum weights easier to check if the expressions named the fields. `Txid::size() + sizeof(COutPoint::n)` shows where the 36 comes from, and `GetSizeOfCompactSize(0)` gives the empty script’s length prefix in both cases.

support.reason: Makes sense to keep just these two commits and leave peer disconnect handling for undeserializable messages to a follow-up.

I’m glad you dropped the weight accounting and stream state - I was uneasy about touching that much serialization code for this, and the two remaining checks are much easier to review. I also prefer reserve with emplace_back here, filling each entry just after construction seems cache-friendlier - and it was slightly faster when I timed block decoding locally.

result.notes: Dropped deleted commenter Husteem and their claim. Added l0rinc as a supporting reviewer with an ACK, along with several suggestions covering test coverage, bounds margins, documentation, and parsing extraction.
